title: Local factorization of $f^!$ on an affine chart
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p_0>0$ with $p_0\ne\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with the following condensed coefficient convention. For $E$, the coefficient ring has sections $S\mapsto C(S,E)$ on profinite sets, with the $\ell$-adic topology, as in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], whose sections on a profinite set $S$ are the continuous maps $S\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with image contained in some finite subextension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Use the module-object pro-etale categories $\Dbc(-,\Lambda)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], their localizing closures [sk-def-localizing-closure], and the exceptional right adjoints of [sk-prop-sf-existence]. Write $a^*=La^*$ for derived pullback [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ and $u:U\hookrightarrow X$ be affine open subschemes with $f(U)\subset V$, let $d\ge0$, let $i:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_V$ be a closed immersion over $V$, and let $p:\mathbf A^d_V\to V$ be the projection [def-sbc-affine-space], so $fu=vpi$. Then there is an isomorphism of functors
$$
u^*f^!\simeq i^!p^!v^*:\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dbc(U,\Lambda)),
$$
and $u^*f^!K\in\Dbc(U,\Lambda)$ for every $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$. There exists a finite family of such data $(V,U,i,d)$ whose opens $U$ cover $X$.

proof.text: Install Noetherianity and compactness from finite type over the field. Give affine opens their composite structure maps to Spec k. Open immersions are separated and locally of finite type, and are quasi-compact here. The finite-dimensional affine-space projection is separated and of finite type. Its composite structure map and the closed immersion therefore satisfy the standing hypotheses. The complement of the closed immersion is quasi-compact because its ambient scheme is Noetherian.

proof.text: Choose auxiliary compactifications for i followed by p and for u followed by f. Their localizing preservation is det-sf-comp-coherence-single. Apply lem-sfb-localizing-lower-shriek-composition to (i,p), (pi,v), and (u,f), with hqi and hq identifying the total morphisms. Their composite gives (Li followed by Lp) followed by Lv isomorphic to Lu followed by Lf. Composite adjunctions and right-adjoint uniqueness then give Ff followed by Su isomorphic to Sv followed by Fp followed by Fi, on the whole localizing categories.

Compare arbitrary compactifications by det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle and arbitrary right adjoints by uniqueness. Apply the coefficient transport above for an arbitrary isomorphic coefficient presentation.

proof.text: For the closed immersion, compare its chosen compactification to (id,i) by det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle. Extension by zero along the identity is the identity, and exact direct image agrees with its derived functor, giving the closed normalization required by det-prop-closed-adjoint-constructible-yoneda. The support assertions are sk-lem-formal-closed-support. The Yoneda comparison identifies Fi on bounded constructible objects with derived closed support. lem-sfb-rational-closed-support-constructible proves support preserves the finite-constant-model bounded-constructible property for both canonical rational coefficient rings; coefficient conjugation of the closed direct-image adjunction transports this to the stated isomorphic presentations.

This gives the bounded-constructibility clause.
